observation.visible_scene: A nighttime architectural installation: a gray concrete wall marked with a regular grid of formwork tie-holes, pierced by a large arched opening. From the top edge of the arch a thin sheet of water pours down, forming a translucent vertical curtain that is flooded with saturated blue light. Behind and through the curtain a slender tree with sparse reddish-orange leaves/flowers is visible near the center, a pale curved bar arcs across the opening, and a small bright lamp glows at the lower right. The wall, arch outline, tree and lamp keep the same positions throughout.
visible_changes: The water curtain keeps flowing downward: the brightness, spacing and faint shape of the individual vertical streaks shift subtly from frame to frame, consistent with continuous falling water rather than a static sheet.
The blue illumination on the wall and water stays essentially constant in hue and intensity.
The arched opening, the concrete wall, the tree behind the curtain and the lower-right lamp do not change position, indicating a fixed camera and no object translation.
No onset or completion of any action is visible; the flow is already underway at the first frame and still ongoing at the last.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the water flow began before this excerpt or continues after it.
The source and mechanism of the blue lighting and of the water supply at the arch's top.
Anything behind the wall or beyond the frame edges.
uncertain_details: Any very slight sway of the tree or its foliage cannot be confirmed against the moving water.
Possible minute camera drift is not distinguishable from the changing water texture.
The identity of the curved bar within the opening (structural element vs. pipe) is not determinable.
